selection: proprietary software reasons that cause costs
description: The most relevant reasons why proprietary software causes costs, each linked to proprietary software with 'can cause' and quantified by the studies and official statements that report it for the world and per country: the licence cost, with the Microsoft licences of the German federal government (answer of the federal government to Rebecca Lenhard, reported by the Stuttgarter Zeitung 2026) and the licence cost avoided by the open-source migrations of Munich (LiMux cost comparison 2012) and Schleswig-Holstein (state government 2025); the licence price change, with the Microsoft 365 price increase of July 2026 (Microsoft 2025); the hardware upgrade forced by a new proprietary operating system, avoided by Munich; and the vendor lock-in, with the one-time switching cost of Schleswig-Holstein. The benefit of open-source software is stated as what it is, the cost that proprietary software would add or the value it would not create, and not as a cost of proprietary software: the economic impact of open-source software on the EU economy (Blind et al. 2021), the demand-side value of open-source software for the firms of the world (Hoffmann, Nagle & Zhou 2024), the value of Apache that the US statistics do not measure (Greenstein & Nagle 2014) and the productivity gain of free open-source software (Nagle 2019). The security failures of closed code are shown by the Storm-0558 intrusion into Microsoft Exchange Online (CSRB 2024) and the CrowdStrike outage of 2024 (Parametrix 2024); these values are not attributed to proprietary software by their sources, because the sources name the security culture of the vendor and a faulty update as the cause, so they do not carry a '<reason> due to proprietary software' triple. The assumed public licence spending, the annual loss and the solution are stated in problem_proprietary_software.json instead, because they are the row of the global problem ranking of the start page. Every number is taken from the named source as reported; a country that a source does not report is left out and never estimated. A share is stored as the decimal ratio, a loss as a positive number and a change with its sign. Each study has its own scope and metric, so numbers of different studies are not comparable without reading the source description; e.g. the demand-side value of Hoffmann et al. is the cost of a hypothetical world in which every firm rebuilds the open-source software it uses, not a measured loss. Every amount of money is stated in euro: the US dollar figure of the source is converted with the ECB 2023 annual average of 1.0813 USD per EUR (the value of GDP.json) whatever the price base year of the source, and the source figure is kept in the description of the value. A value of a reason carries the triple '<reason> due to proprietary software' and not the phrase 'proprietary software' itself, because a value that names a global problem directly is a row of the global problem ranking of the start page, where only the potential loss and the solution of a problem belong.

sources.name: Stuttgarter Zeitung (2026) Bund gibt 2025 über 481 Millionen Euro für Microsoft-Lizenzen aus
sources.description: Brauer, M., AFP (2026): Geld spielt offenbar keine Rolle: Bund gibt 2025 über 481 Millionen Euro für Microsoft-Lizenzen aus. Stuttgarter Zeitung, 9 February 2026. Reports the answer of the German federal government to a written question of the Green member of the Bundestag Rebecca Lenhard: Microsoft products worth 274.1 million EUR were called up in 2023, 347.7 million EUR in 2024 and 481.4 million EUR for licences in 2025; the comparability with earlier answers is limited, because the group of entitled users extends beyond the ministries and their subordinate agencies.

sources.name: Microsoft (2025) Microsoft 365 packaging and pricing updates 2026
sources.description: Microsoft (2025): Microsoft 365 packaging and pricing updates, announced 4 December 2025, effective 1 July 2026, commercial list prices in USD per user and month: Microsoft 365 E3 from 36.00 to 39.00 (8 percent), Microsoft 365 E5 from 57.00 to 60.00 (5 percent), Microsoft 365 F3 from 8.00 to 10.00 (25 percent); existing customers keep the current price until renewal.

sources.name: Le Monde Informatique (2012) Munich LiMux cost comparison
sources.description: Elyan, J., IDG NS (2012): Munich économise 11 millions d'euros en passant à Linux. Le Monde Informatique, 27 November 2012. Reports the cost comparison published by the city of Munich for the migration of about 11'000 users: the migration to LiMux and OpenOffice cost 22.8 million EUR, a migration to Windows 7 and Office 2010 would have cost a little over 34 million EUR and one to Windows 7 and OpenOffice 29.9 million EUR; LiMux saved 6.8 million EUR of software licences compared to Microsoft Office on Windows 7 and 4.7 million EUR of hardware upgrades, because LiMux runs on the existing hardware. A study of HP for Microsoft disputed the savings but was never published.

sources.name: Schleswig-Holstein (2025) Digitale Souveränität ist möglich und wirtschaftlich
sources.description: State government of Schleswig-Holstein, Ministry of Digitalisation (2025): Digitale Souveränität ist möglich und wirtschaftlich, 4 December 2025. The switch to open-source software saves more than 15 million EUR of licence costs, against nine million EUR of one-time investments planned for 2026 for the migration and the development of the open-source solutions; nearly 80 percent of all workplaces outside the tax administration use LibreOffice. heise online (7 December 2025) reports the 15 million EUR as the saving of 2026 alone, with similar amounts in the following years.

sources.name: Blind et al. (2021) The impact of Open Source Software and Hardware on the EU economy
sources.description: Blind, K., Böhm, M., Grzegorzewska, P., Katz, A., Muto, S., Pätsch, S., Schubert, T. (2021): The impact of Open Source Software and Hardware on technological independence, competitiveness and innovation in the EU economy. Final study report for the European Commission, DG CONNECT. Companies located in the EU invested around 1 billion EUR in open-source software in 2018, which resulted in an impact on the European economy of between 65 and 95 billion EUR; the cost-benefit ratio is above 1:4; an increase of 10 percent of the open-source contributions would annually generate an additional 0.4 to 0.6 percent GDP and more than 600 additional ICT start-ups; by procuring open-source instead of proprietary software the public sector could reduce the total cost of ownership and avoid vendor lock-in.

sources.name: Hoffmann, Nagle & Zhou (2024) The Value of Open Source Software
sources.description: Hoffmann, M., Nagle, F., Zhou, Y. (2024): The Value of Open Source Software. Harvard Business School Strategy Unit Working Paper 24-038, not peer reviewed. Based on the Census II of free and open source software and BuiltWith: the supply-side value, the cost to recreate the most widely used open-source software once, is 4.15 billion USD, while the demand-side value, the cost if every firm had to rebuild the open-source software it uses, is 8.8 trillion USD; firms would need to spend 3.5 times more on software than they currently do if open-source software did not exist.

sources.name: Greenstein & Nagle (2014)
sources.description: Greenstein, S., Nagle, F. (2014): Digital dark matter and the economic contribution of Apache. Research Policy 43(4), 623-631. Based on a 1 percent sample of all outward-facing web servers in the United States, the use of Apache potentially accounts for a mismeasurement of somewhere between 2 and 12 billion USD, between 1.3 and 8.7 percent of the stock of prepackaged software in the private fixed investment of the United States.

sources.name: Nagle (2019) Open Source Software and Firm Productivity
sources.description: Nagle, F. (2019): Open Source Software and Firm Productivity. Management Science 65(3), 1191-1215. Free open-source software has a positive and significant value-added return for firms with an ecosystem of complementary capabilities and none for firms without it; for these firms a 1 percent increase in the use of free open-source software leads to an increase of the value-added productivity of between 0.002 and 0.008 percent; the effect is smaller for larger firms.

sources.name: CSRB (2024) Review of the Summer 2023 Microsoft Exchange Online Intrusion
sources.description: Cyber Safety Review Board (2024): Review of the Summer 2023 Microsoft Exchange Online Intrusion, 20 March 2024. The threat actor Storm-0558 compromised the Microsoft Exchange Online mailboxes of 22 enterprise organizations and 503 related personal accounts worldwide and downloaded approximately 60'000 emails from the US State Department alone; the intrusion was preventable and succeeded because of a cascade of security failures at Microsoft, whose security culture was inadequate and requires an overhaul.

sources.name: Parametrix (2024) CrowdStrike's impact on the Fortune 500
sources.description: Parametrix (2024): CrowdStrike's impact on the Fortune 500. The total direct financial loss facing the US Fortune 500 companies, excluding Microsoft, from the CrowdStrike outage of 19 July 2024 is 5.4 billion USD.
